books.section: Topic 1.6 Cultural Interactions Between Europeans, Native Americans, and Africans
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

primary_sources: Hernando Cortes, Second Letter to Charles V (1520), public domain

options.text: Native peoples agreed that their idols were false.
options.misconception: They believed the idols gave them gifts; they feared what would happen if the idols were mistreated.

options.text: Native peoples had no religious practices of their own.
options.misconception: The passage describes idols, temples, and priests; their religion was central to their lives.

options.text: Native peoples defended their religious practices against Spanish imposition.
Native peoples welcomed the Christian images Cortes set up.
options.misconception: The passage says they remonstrated, which means they objected, not welcomed.

rationales.general:
1. Read what the inhabitants do. They remonstrate, which means they protest.
2. Ask what they are protesting. Cortes has cast down their idols and set up Christian images.
3. Ask what they fear. They fear the idols will grow angry and withhold their gifts.
4. Name the pattern. Protest against an imposed religion is a defense of their own.
Remember: when a source shows people objecting, the objection itself is the evidence of what they valued.
rationales.C: Montezuma and the inhabitants object when their idols are cast down. They warn that the people will rise and that the idols will withhold their gifts, which is a defense of their own religion.
rationales.A: They believed the idols bestowed all temporal good. They feared angering them, which is the opposite of agreeing they were false.
rationales.B: The temple, the idols, and the priests all show a living religion. Cortes would have had nothing to tear down otherwise.
rationales.D: Remonstrate means to protest. The passage shows objection, not welcome.

stem: In the passage, Montezuma and the inhabitants remonstrate when Cortes replaces their idols. What does their response best show?

stimulus.source_note: Hernando Cortes, Second Letter to Charles V, October 30, 1520, public domain; quoted in 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 6.
stimulus.text: I precipitated [the idols] from their pedestals, and cast them down the steps of the temple, purifying the chapels in which they had stood, as they were all polluted with human blood, shed in the sacrifices. In the places of these I put images of our Lady and the Saints, which excited not a little feeling in Muteczuma and the inhabitants, who at first remonstrated, declaring that if my proceedings were known throughout the country, the people would rise against me; for they believed that their idols bestowed on them all temporal good, and if they permitted them to be ill-treated, they would be angry and withhold their gifts. ... I answered, through the interpreters, that they were deceived in expecting any favors from idols, the work of their own hands, formed of unclean things; and that they must learn there was but one God, the universal Lord of all, who had created the heavens and earth, and all things else, and had made them and us.
